title: A maximal Cohen–Macaulay module over a regular local ring is free
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] of Krull dimension $d$, and let $M$ be a finite $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] which is maximal Cohen–Macaulay, i.e. $\operatorname{depth}(M)=d$ [def-weil-pbc-depth]. Then $M$ is a free $R$-module: $M\cong R^{\oplus r}$ for some integer $r\ge0$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00NT (lemma-regular-mcm-free, line 25800), with Definition Tag 00NF (definition-maximal-CM, line 25135)

proof.text: (Setup and the inductive claim.) By definition [def-weil-regular-scheme] a regular local ring $(R,\mathfrak m)$ of dimension $d$ is a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] of Krull dimension $d$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] whose maximal ideal is generated by $d$ elements. A finite $R$-module $M$ with $\operatorname{depth}(M)=d$ is nonzero: for $M=0$ one has $\mathfrak mM=M$, so $\operatorname{depth}(0)=\infty\neq d$ by the definition of depth [def-weil-pbc-depth]. We prove by induction on $d\ge0$ the claim $P(d)$: for every regular local ring $(R,\mathfrak m)$ of dimension $d$ and every finite $R$-module $M$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] with $\operatorname{depth}(M)=d$, $M$ is a free $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-free-module] with a finite basis, $M\cong R^{\oplus r}$. (Stacks writes 'by induction on $\dim(R)$'; the claim is quantified over all such $R$ because the inductive step applies it to the quotient ring $R/xR$.)

(Base case $d=0$.) The maximal ideal is generated by $0$ elements, so $\mathfrak m=0$; a local ring whose maximal ideal is $0$ is a field (every non-unit lies in $\mathfrak m=0$). Hence $M$ is a vector space over the field $R$ and is free by [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-free] (Stacks 09FN). A basis of the finite module $M$ is finite: each of finitely many generators of $M$ is a combination of finitely many basis vectors, so finitely many basis vectors span $M$, and by linear independence (over the nonzero ring $R$) no other basis vector can exist. So $M\cong R^{\oplus r}$.

(Inductive step, $d\ge1$: choice of $x$ and the ring $R/xR$.) Assume $P(d-1)$ and let $R$, $M$ be as in $P(d)$. Choose generators $x_1,\dots,x_d$ of $\mathfrak m$ (a regular system of parameters) and put $x=x_1\in\mathfrak m$; this is the element 'part of a regular sequence generating $\mathfrak m$' of Stacks' proof. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence] (Stacks 00NQ) with $c=1$, $R/xR$ is a regular local ring of dimension $d-1$.

($M$ is Cohen–Macaulay of support dimension $d$, and $\dim(\operatorname{Supp}(M)\cap V(x))=d-1$.) Here $\operatorname{Supp}(N)$ is the set of primes $\mathfrak p$ with $N_{\mathfrak p}
e0$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] and $\dim$ of a set of primes is the supremum of lengths of chains of primes in it. Since $M
e0$ (Step 1), [lem-weil-pbc-depth-le-support-dimension] (Stacks 00LK) gives $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M)\ge\operatorname{depth}(M)=d$; a chain of primes in $\operatorname{Supp}(M)$ is a chain of primes of $R$, so $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M)\le\dim R=d$. Thus $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M)=d=\operatorname{depth}(M)$: $M$ is Cohen–Macaulay. Upper bound: the primes of $R$ containing $x$ correspond, order-preservingly, to the primes of $R/xR$, so $\dim(\operatorname{Supp}(M)\cap V(x))\le\dim V(x)=\dim(R/xR)=d-1$ by Step 3. Lower bound: by [lem-weil-pbc-support-dimension-quotient-element-bound] (Stacks 0B52, second inequality) $d=\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M)\le\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M/xM)+1$; and $\operatorname{Supp}(M/xM)\subseteq\operatorname{Supp}(M)\cap V(x)$, because for $x
otin\mathfrak p$ the element $x$ is a unit of $R_{\mathfrak p}$ acting by $0$ on $(M/xM)_{\mathfrak p}$, so $(M/xM)_{\mathfrak p}=0$, and for $M_{\mathfrak p}=0$ the quotient $(M/xM)_{\mathfrak p}$ of $M_{\mathfrak p}$ vanishes. Hence $\dim(\operatorname{Supp}(M)\cap V(x))\ge d-1$, so it equals $d-1=\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M)-1$. (This is the hypothesis $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M/xM)=\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M)-1$ under which Stacks applies Proposition 00N6 with $c=1$.)

($x$ is a nonzerodivisor on $M$, and $\operatorname{depth}_R(M/xM)=d-1$.) By Step 4, $R$ is Noetherian local, $M\ne0$ is finite and Cohen–Macaulay, $x\in\mathfrak m$ and $\dim(\operatorname{Supp}(M)\cap V(x))=\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M)-1$. So [lem-weil-pbc-cm-module-good-element-nonzerodivisor] (Stacks 00N5, the case $c=1$ of Proposition 00N6 that Stacks cites) gives (a) $x$ is a nonzerodivisor on $M$, and (b) $\operatorname{depth}(M/xM)=\operatorname{depth}(M)-1=d-1$, the depth taken over $R$.

($M/xM$ is maximal Cohen–Macaulay over $R/xR$.) Write $\bar R=R/xR$, $\bar{\mathfrak m}=\mathfrak m/xR$ and $N=M/xM$, a finite $\bar R$-module ($x$ kills $N$; the images of generators of $M$ generate $N$). The depth of $N$ over $\bar R$ equals its depth over $R$ (definition of depth [def-weil-pbc-depth] and of regular sequences [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]): for $f\in R$ with image $\bar f$, multiplication by $\bar f$ and by $f$ on any quotient of $N$ is the same map, and $(\bar f_1,\dots,\bar f_i)N=(f_1,\dots,f_i)N$; so $f_1,\dots,f_r\in\mathfrak m$ is $N$-regular over $R$ iff $\bar f_1,\dots,\bar f_r\in\bar{\mathfrak m}$ is $N$-regular over $\bar R$, every sequence in $\bar{\mathfrak m}$ lifts to one in $\mathfrak m$, and $\bar{\mathfrak m}N=\mathfrak mN$. Hence $\operatorname{depth}_{\bar R}(N)=d-1=\dim\bar R$ by Steps 3 and 5.

(Conclusion.) By Steps 3 and 6, $\bar R=R/xR$ is regular local of dimension $d-1$ and $M/xM$ is a finite $\bar R$-module of depth $d-1$, so $M/xM$ is a free $R/xR$-module by the induction hypothesis $P(d-1)$. Since $R$ is Noetherian local, $x\in\mathfrak m$, $M$ is finite and $x$ is a nonzerodivisor on $M$ (Step 5), [lem-weil-pbc-free-mod-nonzerodivisor] (Stacks 00NS, 'we win by Lemma 00NS') shows that $M$ is a free $R$-module; its basis is finite as in Step 2, so $M\cong R^{\oplus r}$. This proves $P(d)$ and the lemma.

Statement kept; def-weil-pbc-free-module added to stmt_deps (the conclusion 'free'). The Stacks proof leaves implicit that M ≠ 0, that the depth of M/xM over R/xR equals its depth over R, and the dimension hypothesis of 00N6; these are written out.
